subject: Nanotechnology
title: Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
description: A micro-lesson that makes Transition Metal Dichalcogenides usable.

hook.text: Peel molybdenum disulfide down to a single layer and it becomes a semiconductor with a natural band gap.

buildup.text: TMDs like MoS₂ and WSe₂ are atomically thin semiconductors — each layer is just three atoms thick.

discovery.text: Unlike graphene, monolayer TMDs switch off cleanly — ideal for ultra-thin transistors.

twist.text: Contact resistance where metal meets the TMD is enormous — injecting current into a 2D sheet is hard.

climax.text: TSMC and Intel are evaluating TMD channels for transistors beyond the 1 nm node — 2D may replace 3D silicon.

punchline.text: Three atoms thick and it still switches — the thinnest transistor channel possible.

quiz.question: What advantage do TMDs have over graphene for transistors?
options: They have a natural band gap that allows clean on/off switching
They conduct electricity faster than graphene
